best_for: Owners of Bambu Lab printers, especially those with an AMS for multi-color prints, who want the slicer the printer was tuned for and the option to send and watch jobs from the desktop.

points.title: Built for Bambu printers, from PrusaSlicer
points.text: Bambu Studio started from PrusaSlicer, which itself comes from Slic3r. It ships profiles for Bambu Lab machines, and the project says it also supports other printers, but the README does not list which ones.

points.title: Project files with many plates
points.text: A project can hold several build plates, with auto-arrange and auto-orient. Settings work at the project, object and part level, and there are tree, hybrid and custom supports, painting tools for multi-material prints and STEP file import.

points.title: The network plugin is not open source
points.text: The slicer is AGPL-3.0, but remote control and monitoring rely on an optional plugin built on non-free libraries. Without it, you can still slice and carry the file to the printer on an SD card.

points.title: Release 2.9.1 adds mixed nozzles
points.text: The 2.9.1 release can print parts of one model with different nozzle diameters and layer heights. That needs the H3C printer for now; the notes say other models will follow.

points.title: Linux: AppImage or verified Flatpak
points.text: Bambu Lab publishes AppImages built for Ubuntu and Fedora and points everyone else to Flathub. The Flathub build covers x64 and Arm64 and is marked verified for Bambu Lab, though it is a large download of about 450 MB.

points.title: Versions kept on this site
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 33 versions, as a machine-wide installer or a zip, which helps if a new release changes a profile you depend on. macOS (a universal build) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
